## Analysis

Sol_0027 confirms that direct coordinate perturbations also leave the `q=56` incumbent unchanged, so the plateau is not merely an artifact of tensor membership. Together with sol_0024–0026, local additions, swaps, geometric moves, and row/column reconstructions are now strongly disfavored. One important neighborhood remains untested on the improved sol_0023 lineage: systematic sparsification. The earlier deletion beam used the weaker 2,244-span tensor parent; deleting points from the nonlinear 1,881-span embedding may preserve its unusually compressed difference set while improving both normalized ratios.

## Next

Embed sol_0023 as fallback, then run a width-32 marginal-deletion beam from `n=277` down to `n=80`, scoring all single deletions exactly and retaining distinct canonical states. After every 8 deletions, perform 2,000 tabu-guided delete/add repairs with replacement coordinates in `[0,1881]`; use seed `5028`, a 155-second deadline, and atomic strict-improvement checkpoints.
